attacked.target: The receipt of 2,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset, taxed at 30% under s.115BBH. The value is determined on the settlement date (2026-06-23) using the telegraphic transfer buying rate. No TDS is required as the recipient is outside India. Under s.439(8), a bona fide disclosure of the income with all material facts is required to avoid penalties.
attacked.attack: This conclusion depends on the 'declaration_of_service_payment', 'income_tax_deduction', and 'valuation_date', all of which are missing. Asserting the conclusion despite these dependencies being unmet is incorrect.

attacked.target: The valuation date is the settlement date (2026-06-23) as per Rule 56
attacked.attack: Rule 56 does not apply to the valuation of virtual digital assets for the purpose of s.115BBH. The opening words of Rule 56 specify that it applies to the determination of fair market value for specific sections, none of which include s.115BBH.
